messages.text: Is there a guarentee?

Yes — Replogle globes are backed by the manufacturer's warranty against defects in materials and workmanship for one year from purchase (90 days for electronic components like lights or AR features). If anything arrives damaged or develops a defect, reaching out within 48 hours of noticing it gets you a replacement or refund with no extra cost, including return shipping. You can find the full details on the Refund & Return Policy page on our site. Is there a specific globe you're looking at that you want to make sure is covered?
I am wondering if the Blue or Antique Globe is easier to see the details on the globe

The blue ocean globes give you that crisp, bright, classic look with high contrast between land and sea, so text and borders tend to pop and are easy to read at a glance — great if you want quick, clear reading. The antique ocean globes have warm, sepia-toned seas for a vintage, old-world feel, which makes the detail feel more like exploring a treasured map, rich and textured rather than high-contrast. Are you picking between two specific globes, or just deciding on the overall look first?
I am looking at the 16" globe

For easiest reading, the Trafalgar 16-inch Blue Ocean Floor Globe is a great pick — its bright blue ocean and crisp colour contrast make the country borders, place names, and text especially easy to read at a glance, and it's hand-assembled with raised relief for feel-the-mountains texture too. If you love a warmer, vintage look for the same size, the Commander II 16" Antique Ocean Floor Globe gives that rich sepia-toned detail instead. Would this be going into a home office, living room, or somewhere else?
Going into my home, probably the TV rooom

Perfect spot for it — a 16" floor globe like the Trafalgar makes a nice visual anchor near a TV room without overwhelming the space, and the bright blue ocean map will stay easy to read even from across the room. You'll find it under "Trafalgar 16-inch Blue Ocean Floor Globe - Handcrafted Raised Relief" in the search bar, ready to add to your cart. Was it the bright, easy-to-read look that sold you, or were you weighing it against something else too?
No I am looking at the 16" "desk" version.  Does that come in the blue and antique option?

Yes — the Eureka 16" comes in both: the Eureka 16" Antique Ocean Desktop Globe with Full-Swing Metal Meridian gives you that warm, vintage look, and the Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe with Black Metal Gyromatic Base gives you the bright, easy-to-read classic map, both at $234.75 and both sized for a desk rather than the floor. Given what you said about wanting detail to be easy to see, the blue ocean version would likely suit you best. Would this be for your own desk, or is it a gift?
Just to be clear, do both of the 16" globes rotate?
Opened a product
Searched the catalog · Eureka 16 inch globe

Yes, both do — the Eureka Antique has a full-swing metal gyromatic meridian that lets you tilt and rotate the sphere to any region (including the poles) and lock it in place, and the Eureka Blue Ocean has that same full gyromatic mounting for smooth rotation on both the vertical and horizontal axes. So whichever colour you go with, you'll get full multi-directional spin.
So I can put Australia at the top for viewing for instance?

Exactly — since both the antique and blue ocean Eureka 16" use that full-swing gyromatic meridian, you can tilt the sphere on its axis and lock it at any angle, so turning Australia (or any region) to the top for a closer look is no problem. Given what you mentioned about wanting details easy to read, the Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe would be the one to go with — you'll find it under that name in search, ready to add to your cart.
How current are the countries?

The product description for the Eureka says it features up-to-date political boundaries, balancing the antique-style look with current geographic data — it's not stated to a specific year, though. If you'd like the exact cartography date it was last updated, that's worth confirming with (email hidden) before you order. Want me to flag that for you, or are you ready to move ahead with the Blue Ocean version?
Is there other information on the globe besides country name?

Yes — the Eureka's cartography goes beyond country names, with over 4,000 place names and points of interest shown, plus up-to-date political boundaries throughout. The listing doesn't break down every category beyond that (like specific waterways or cap····), so if you want a full list of what's labeled, (email hidden) can confirm. Does that level of detail sound like what you're after for this one?
Yes one of the reasons for ordering the larger globe is to hopefully get additinal detail on the globe.

That makes sense — at 16" with over 4,000 place names and raised relief terrain, the Eureka gives you noticeably more room for detail than a 12" desk globe, so it's a solid choice for that goal. You'll find it under "Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe - Black Metal Gyromatic Base" in search, ready to add to your cart. Is this one going to a home office, or somewhere else in the house?

Either spot would suit it well — the Eureka's black metal gyromatic base gives it a clean, modern look that works equally well on an office desk or as a conversation piece in an entertainment room.
